name: Carlos Alexandre Pontes Pizzino
headline: Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering (Robotics and Control Systems) | Robotics Engineer

sections.title: Professional summary
paragraphs: I design, integrate, and validate autonomous robotic systems for complex real-world environments. My work combines robotics software architecture, SLAM, multisensor fusion, navigation, perception, and decision-making, with a strong focus on systems that must operate reliably outside controlled laboratory conditions. I hold a PhD in Electrical Engineering, specialising in Control, Automation and Robotics, and bring more than 15 years of experience across applied research, systems engineering, technical leadership, and field deployment. My expertise lies in defining and leading end-to-end autonomy architectures, transforming advanced research components into coherent, robust, and maintainable robotic systems. This includes managing system-level trade-offs across perception, localisation, navigation, decision-making, communications, computational constraints, and operational safety.

entries.title: I-DEAL: Smarter Geospatial Data for a Sustainable Europe
entries.funding: EU-funded Horizon Europe, Grant agreement ID: 101236355
bullets: I-DEAL is an EU-funded project supported by the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) – Staff Exchanges, advancing geospatial technologies for the Green Deal and climate change mitigation.
I undertook a one-month secondment at Fondazione Bruno Kessler (FBK) in Trento, Italy.
The objectives were to investigate a modular multimodal SLAM frontend combining LiDAR, IMU, stereo vision and GNSS-RTK and develop sensor-trust indicators for reliable localisation and mapping.

entries.title: REMORA: Swarm Robotics for the Improvement and Observation of Aquatic Resources
bullets: REMORA is a project focused on improving aquatic resource management in Portugal and the EU through swarm robotics and digital twins, targeting TRL 6 for the blue economy.
As a robotic engineer, I develop software for swarm robotic systems, focusing on coordination, communication, and collective behaviour in distributed robotics.

entries.title: HARD-HAT: Socially aware navigation for safer heavy-duty construction
entries.funding: Collaborative project of the European euROBIN project / Horizon Europe Programme Project 101070596
bullets: HARD-HAT aims to integrate the Cooperative Human-Aware Navigation (CoHAN) framework for controlling heavy robots, alongside rule-based Natural Language Understanding.
As a Senior Robotics Engineer, I lead the integration of the CoHAN planner and rule-based NLU modules on heavy robotic platforms.

entries.title: CRIARTE: Construction with Intelligent Robotics and Revolutionary Architecture of Emerging Technologies
bullets: CRIARTE integrates mobile robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Digital Twins, and augmented reality within the construction sector to enable large-scale autonomous robots to collaborate with humans.
As a robotic engineer, I design and implement real-time navigation algorithms for dynamic environments using C++, Python, and ROS Noetic, integrating mapping, localisation, and perception.

entries.title: FORTIS: Multi-Modal and Multi-Aspect Holistic Human-Robot Interaction
entries.funding: EU-funded Horizon Europe, Grant agreement ID: 101135707
bullets: FORTIS is an EU-funded project focused on enabling long-term, human-like interaction between robots and humans.

As a robotic engineer, I design and implement navigation and perception algorithms for an Autonomous Pallet Loader using C++, Python, and ROS, enabling real-time obstacle avoidance and route optimisation in dynamic environments.

entries.title: OpenSwarm: Orchestration and Programming ENergy-aware and collaborative Swarms With AI-powered Reliable Methods
entries.funding: EU-funded Horizon Europe, Grant agreement ID: 101093046
bullets: OpenSwarm is an EU-funded project advancing collaborative and distributed intelligent node technologies.

As a robotic engineer, I integrated ROS-based autonomy software with PX4/Pixhawk flight controllers via MAVROS/MAVLink, supporting autonomous waypoint navigation, mission execution, telemetry monitoring, and multi-UAV operations. Participated actively in consortium meetings and EU reviews.

entries.title: FEROX: Fostering and Enabling AI, Data and Robotics Tech for Supporting Human Workers in Harvesting Wild Food
entries.funding: EU-funded Horizon Europe, Grant agreement ID: 101070440
bullets: FEROX is an EU-funded project applying AI, data, and robotics to improve working conditions for wild fruit harvesters and optimise harvesting operations.
As a robotic engineer, I developed UAV-based mapping, localisation, and perception algorithms using PX4/Pixhawk integration through ROS/MAVROS and the CTU Multi-Robot Systems framework.

entries.title: SafeForest: Semi-Autonomous Robotic System for Forest Cleaning and Fire Prevention
bullets: SafeForest is a project developing advanced robotic systems for forest fire prevention and urban–forest interface monitoring.
As a robotic engineer, I implemented tightly coupled LiDAR inertial odometry with smoothing and real-time mapping for robot state estimation.

entries.title: NeoSLAM: Long-term Visual SLAM using Computational Models of the Brain
entries.organisation: Federal University of Rio de Janeiro and Heriot-Watt University
bullets: NeoSLAM is a novel hybrid computational model which is inspired by the hippocampal–neocortical network for Visual Place Recognition used in SLAM and (re-)localization systems in changing conditions.
I work on the development of the model and software based on Python, C++, MATLAB, ROS/Gazebo with the Clearpath Husky robot.

entries.title: Flight inspection of NavAids using UAS
entries.organisation: Brazilian Air Force – Institute of Airspace Control
bullets: The aim of this project is to analyse the use of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) for field measurements required for commissioning and regular maintenance of Instrument Landing Systems (ILS).
In this project, I developed MATLAB codes for path planning.

entries.title: LAICA
entries.organisation: Brazilian Air Force – Department of Airspace Control
bullets: LAICA is an automatic calibration system which allows calibration of a large number of electrical sourcing and measuring instruments. It drastically reduced the calibration time of many electrical testing equipment and electrical meters.

In this project, I managed a team of two Electronics Engineers and three technicians. Besides, I developed software based on LabVIEW. In 2018, I was recognised for exemplary performance and contributions to the Brazilian Airspace Control.

entries.title: DIANE
bullets: DIANE is an Explosive Ordnance Disposal Robot and was constituted of tracks for locomotion, arms to climb and descend stairs, a robotic manipulator of 3 DOF to manipulate the explosive, and cameras for operation.
I worked on the electronic architecture based on a Puma PC/104-Plus single board computer with QNX, EPOS positioning controllers by Maxon and CANopen.
